old_description: Selhorst Woodworks was built on a shared vision between husband-and-wife team Matthew and Chantel Selhorst: to create exceptional spaces through thoughtful design, expert craftsmanship, and an unwavering commitment to quality.
about:
Selhorst Woodworks operates from Las Vegas, Nevada, where husband-and-wife founders Matthew and Chantel Selhorst established the family-owned business on a shared vision to create exceptional spaces through thoughtful design and expert craftsmanship. What began as a passion for woodworking has grown into a custom finish carpentry company serving the Las Vegas area from its facility on East Patrick Lane.

The shop specializes in custom-milled architectural woodwork including accent walls, accent ceilings, barn doors, shelving, built-ins, mudrooms, baseboards, crown molding, and structural beams. The team also works with specialty materials such as Thermory thermally modified wood and Renson products, and provides design services and wallpaper installation. Projects range from single-room focal points to whole-home millwork packages.

Clients include homeowners, interior designers, builders, and architects who value timeless design and meticulous attention to detail. The company collaborates directly with design professionals and general contractors on residential new-build and renovation projects throughout the Las Vegas market.

The Selhorsts emphasize a family-first approach, treating each project with the same care they would apply in their own home. They position the business on a seamless client experience from initial consultation through final installation, with a focus on the smallest details that make the biggest impact and craftsmanship intended to stand the test of time.

name: Sentinel Solar
old_description: Sentinel Solar specializes in premium residential solar + storage systems designed for performance, resilience, and longevity. We handle everything from permitting to utility approval, and we build systems we'd put on our own homes.
about:
Sentinel Solar operates from Covington, Kentucky, serving customers across Kentucky and Ohio. The company was founded by Jan Thurman, a solar veteran with over a decade of coast-to-coast experience in residential and commercial system design and installation. Thurman launched the business on a simple conviction: solar should be done right, or not at all, emphasizing precision engineering and long-term craftsmanship over volume.

The firm provides full-service solar and storage solutions, handling every step from initial consultation and custom system design through permitting, utility approval, and professional installation. Each project is tailored to the specific roof, energy usage, and goals of the customer, with ongoing production monitoring and long-term support.

Sentinel Solar works with both homeowners and businesses. Recent installations include a system for Heatherbrook Farms in Fort Mitchell, Kentucky, and a commercial array for Wenzel Distillery in Cincinnati, Ohio. The company also serves residential clients in neighborhoods such as Indian Hill, demonstrating experience across agricultural, industrial, and high-end residential sectors.

Thurman positions the company as a premium alternative to high-volume installers, citing four pillars: a consultative, no-pressure sales process; local accountability as an independent, non-franchise operation; installer-first design that prioritizes crew safety and build quality; and a referral-driven model that ties long-term relationships to sustained performance. The company is licensed and insured in both Kentucky and Ohio.

name: Service Electric Cable TV & Communications - Bethlehem HQ
old_description: An affordable alternative to traditional cable television at only $19.95 per month with hundreds of live bonus channels and NO network fees, cable TV fees, sports channel fees or rental fees!  Bonus channels include more than 70 Spanish language channels, 40+ true crime options, music, news, weather, kids channels and much more!
about:
Service Electric Cable TV & Communications is headquartered in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, where it consolidated operations in 2014. The company traces its origins to 1948, when founder John Walson Sr. (born John Walsonavich) extended a coaxial cable from an antenna atop Broad Mountain to his appliance store in Mahanoy City, creating the first community antenna television system in the United States. Now a third-generation family business, it remains under the leadership of the Walson family, with John M. Walson serving as president since 2012.

The company provides cable television, broadband internet, and telephone services across the Lehigh Valley, Hunterdon County (NJ), and Wilkes-Barre regions. Residential offerings include a low-cost Broadband TV package with hundreds of channels and no hidden fees, plus Gig+ internet speeds paired with eero whole-home WiFi. For commercial customers, Service Electric Business delivers dedicated internet, voice, and cable TV with free local, same-day service calls. The firm also operates the Service Electric Network (SEN), a three-channel local network producing high school and collegiate sports, community events, and festival coverage.

Customers range from individual households to small, medium, and enterprise-level businesses throughout eastern Pennsylvania and western New Jersey. Partnerships with PenTeleData and Alianza extend internet and voice capabilities, while membership in the America's Communications Association and the Broadband Communications Association of Pennsylvania underscores industry engagement.

Service Electric emphasizes its deep community roots and pioneering history—it was the first U.S. cable system to offer Home Box Office in 1972 and among the earliest to deploy two-way cable modems. The company cites its family ownership, local workforce, and commitment to same-day business support as key differentiators in a market dominated by national providers.

name: Service Metal Fabricators
old_description: Service Metal Fabricators is a one-stop shop providing comprehensive precision sheet metal fabrication services for over 40 years. As a full-service fabricator specializing in NEMA and other electronic enclosures, brackets, panels and assemblies, along with stainless steel medical containers, our services have proven integral to a wide range of customers in various industries. Our enclosures often house the printed circuit boards and other internal electronic data processing, controlling and actuating parts for products serving unique purposes in the electronics, industrials, diagnostic/measurement and various other industries.
about:
Service Metal Fabricators operates from Williamsburg, Virginia, where it has provided precision sheet metal fabrication for over 40 years. The company does not disclose its founding year or founders, and ownership details are not publicly stated.

The shop specializes in NEMA-rated electronic enclosures, brackets, panels, assemblies, and stainless-steel medical containers. Its process lineup includes shearing, CNC punching, press-brake forming, vertical milling, MIG/TIG and spot welding, hardware insertion, riveting, mechanical assembly, silk-screening, chemical finishing, powder coating, and painting. Work is performed in a 12-acre, 56,000-square-foot facility (also described as 60,000 square feet) with machine redundancy to support scaling. Headcount is not published, though the quality department maintains a ratio of three QA professionals for every 25 production staff.

Customers span electronics, industrial equipment, diagnostic and measurement devices, medical, aerospace, defense, transportation, solar energy, and TEMPEST computing. Named references include Becton Dickinson’s laboratory blood-analyzer systems, a $15 billion transportation company’s electronics division, an emerging smart-circuitry solar firm, helm stations for a dozen U.S. aircraft carriers, and various components for U.S. armed forces machinery.

The company differentiates itself through vertical integration—operating its own delivery fleet and offering free shipping within 200 miles—in-house design engineering and DFM support, reverse-engineering capability, and a quality program that adheres to ISO guidelines, MIL-DTL-5541, AMS-STD-1595, RoHS, and numerous other military and federal standards.

name: Severance Foods / Pan De Oro
old_description: Pan De Oro is a family owned and operated brand that has been producing delicious tortilla chips for almost 40 years.  Our attention to high-quality standards, all natural ingredients and unique flavors all play a key part in why our chips are so delicious!
about:
Severance Foods, operating under the Pan De Oro brand, has been producing tortilla chips in Hartford, Connecticut since 1985. The company was founded by three food scientists—Richard Stevens, John Grikis, and Rich Dana—who had developed products such as Ortega Mexican Foods for Heublein, Inc. When R.J. Reynolds acquired Heublein in 1984 and planned to relocate operations to California, the trio used their severance packages to establish their own facility in the Northeast, anticipating rising demand for Mexican-style foods in the region.

Today, Severance Foods describes itself as the largest manufacturer and co-packer of tortilla chips in the Northeast. From its plant in Hartford, the company produces its own Pan De Oro line of non‑GMO, organic, hand‑crafted tortilla chips and salsa, while also providing contract manufacturing and co‑packing services for other brands. The operation emphasizes all‑natural ingredients and proprietary flavor development rooted in the founders’ product‑development background.

The company’s customer base spans foodservice, institutional, and retail channels. Pan De Oro products have been supplied to restaurants, schools, and concession stands since 1985, and the brand now appears in grocery stores and farmers markets across New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania.

The founders’ original motivation was to fill a regional supply gap for tortilla products, and the company continues to differentiate itself through a family‑owned, hands‑on approach that prioritizes ingredient transparency—non‑GMO, organic, and free of artificial additives—and a hand‑crafted process that the firm says preserves texture and flavor.
type_evidence: Today, Severance Foods is the largest manufacturer and co-packer of tortilla chips in the northeast.

name: SiCamore Semi
old_description: More efficient drivetrains using semiconductor technologies based on Wide Band Gap (WBG) materials such as Silicon Carbide (SiC) are enabling engineers to achieve high voltage (1.2 – 3.3KV) and high power demands in a cost-effective way.
about:
SiCamore Semi operates a pure-play semiconductor foundry in Bend, Oregon, drawing on more than 30 years of wafer-fabrication experience. The company focuses on wide-bandgap materials such as silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) to serve high-voltage, high-power applications.

The foundry runs 100 mm and 150 mm production lines for silicon and SiC, offering single-step device manufacturing, multi-project wafer (MPW) service, and a dedicated gold fab for high-reliability, radiation-hardened, and RF devices. Process capabilities include photolithography with ASML 5000 I-line steppers and Karl Suss aligners, thin-film deposition (sputtering, PVD, CVD, PECVD, e-beam evaporation), frontside/backside metal stacks, thermal oxidation and diffusion, wet and plasma dry etching, RIE, rapid thermal annealing, and cold/hot ion implantation. SiC-specific steps cover high-temperature implant/anneal and gate oxidation with nitric oxide anneal. Partner services extend to device design, wafer thinning, dicing, packaging, and test.

Customers span electric-vehicle drivetrain suppliers, medical-device makers (monitoring, diagnostic, therapeutic), industrial OEMs in agriculture, data centers, energy, and robotics, aerospace and defense programs requiring ITAR-compliant fabrication, and academic partners collaborating on NASA, NSF, DOE, and DOD grants. The company supplies SiC diodes, MOSFETs, JBSFETs, JFETs, IGBTs, Si SGTOs, and SDIODEs to these markets.

SiCamore Semi states its mission is to deliver innovative power-semiconductor solutions through silicon, SiC, GaN, and photonics technologies, aiming to become the wide-bandgap fabrication facility in the U.S. Northwest for both government agencies and commercial sectors such as transportation, telecommunications, and healthcare infrastructure.

old_description: At Sierra Metals Southwest LLC, we specialize in crafting exceptional architectural and ornamental metals in the Las Vegas area. With a passion for precision and design, we offer both standard and custom solutions to elevate commercial, residential, or artistic spaces. From intricate details to bold elements our expert team delivers high quality metal work tailored to your vision.
about:
Sierra Metals Southwest LLC operates from a facility on West Oquendo Road in Las Vegas, Nevada. The company was established by owners with more than 40 years of combined experience in metal fabrication and operates as part of a family of companies that includes Andy Russo Jr Inc, a union installation specialist, and Magnus Ornamental Metals, which focuses on residential ornamental work.

The shop produces architectural and ornamental metalwork for commercial, residential, and artistic projects. Capabilities include MIG welding of steel, TIG welding of stainless steel, brass, and aluminum, shearing up to 3/16-inch mild steel at 12-foot lengths, ACM routing, polishing to #4, #6, and #8 finishes, and light-gauge bending up to 16 gauge at 12 feet. The facility also runs water-jet and plasma-cutting systems capable of beveling and 5-axis cutting with taper control, plus CAD support for custom designs. Standard and custom product lines cover fences, gates, handrails, decorative ceilings, door frames, shade panels, louvers, trellises, security screens, art sculptures, ACM panels, and standing-seam metal roofing components.

The company also partners with F&A Modular Homes to design and fabricate metal components for modular housing units, including studio and one-bedroom models.

Sierra Metals emphasizes craftsmanship, innovation, customer focus, and reliability as its guiding principles, aiming to deliver tailored solutions with dependable turnaround for the Las Vegas market and beyond.

about:
Sigla Furniture operates from Los Angeles, California, where the company's roots trace back to 1976 when the founder arrived from Iran. By 1980 he had opened a small woodworking workshop after initially importing Italian music boxes. The business remains a second-generation, family-owned custom furniture manufacturer, now led by the founders' child. In 2022 the company expanded by acquiring JDM Furniture and Unfinished Chairs, adding founder Tom Juhasz and his decades of designer-focused experience.

The workshop produces traditional and transitional dining tables, sofas, chairs, and case goods, all custom-made to order using premium imported materials. Each piece is handcrafted in the Los Angeles facility, with typical production and delivery taking eight to ten weeks from order confirmation.

Sigla serves residential clients, interior designers, and large-scale hospitality projects. Commercial references include the Omni Hotel, the Shade Hotel, and Marriott properties, alongside individual homeowners seeking custom seating, tables, and case goods. The company works from client sketches or existing SKUs, adapting frames, upholstery, and finishes to project requirements.

The company emphasizes heirloom-quality craftsmanship intended to last generations, framing furniture as "a stitch in the tapestry of your family." A one-year Sigla Guarantee covers repairs for normal wear and tear, reflecting the founders' goal to create the last piece of furniture a customer will ever need.

old_description: The Lacing Tape Dispenser is made with the ease of use in mind. It helps keep your workbench organized, without having loose rolls of lacing tape rolling around in the workspace. about:
Silver State Wire & Cable Inc. was founded in 1991 in Sparks, Nevada. The company began as a small value‑added service provider with two employees and three wire‑processing machines dating from the early 1950s. It is certified as a Woman‑Owned Small Business (WOSB) and holds a CAGE code of 01CV1.

The firm specializes in wire processing, cable assembly, wiring harness fabrication, crimping, and supply‑chain services. It also manufactures proprietary products such as the Lacing Tape Dispenser and BRAIDLITE™ braided shielding for space applications. Operations include cutting, kitting, heat‑shrink installation, and thermal‑transfer marking using a SumiMark IV Plus system.

The company cites examples ranging from hobby‑plane builders and satellite integrators to fighter‑jet rewiring programs. Its ITAR registration and AS9100/ISO 9001 certifications enable work on controlled defense and aerospace programs.

The founder’s original focus — delivering quality product at an affordable price — remains central. The company emphasizes its quality system, conflict‑minerals compliance, and adherence to FAR/DFAR flow‑down provisions as key differentiators.

name: Simplex Fabrication Welding and CNC Plasma Cutting
old_description: Hi. My name is Seth Neilson, the owner and welder/fabricator at Simplex Fabrication. 10 years ago, I bought a cheap tig welder off the internet and started teaching myself how to weld on an old Nissan I had in the garage. What started out as a hobby has slowly turned into a passion for me. I love welding and fabricating as well as innovating better ways of doing things. If you have an idea you would like to see brought to life, or you just need some cracks rewelded on your lawnmower, I am your guy.
about:
Simplex Fabrication operates from Woodbine, Maryland, where owner Seth Neilson began the business roughly a decade ago after teaching himself to weld with an inexpensive TIG welder. The venture started as a garage hobby repairing an old Nissan and grew into a full-time fabrication shop. Neilson remains the sole proprietor and primary welder-fabricator.

The shop provides welding, CNC plasma cutting, and general metal fabrication services. Work ranges from rust repair on automotive and equipment parts to one-off custom builds such as a go-kart belt sander and a climbing-saddle hunting tree stand. Neilson handles quoting, fabrication, and finishing himself, keeping the operation lean and flexible.

Customers include hobbyists, equipment owners needing repairs, and individuals with custom project ideas. The shop does not target a specific industry but serves anyone requiring metal fabrication or welding, from small repairs to prototype-level assemblies.

Neilson says the business was born from a passion for welding and a drive to innovate better ways of building things. That mindset shapes the shop's approach: taking a customer's concept and turning it into a finished metal piece, whether it's a cracked lawnmower deck or a novel mechanical design.

Founded in 2015 in Raleigh, North Carolina, SinnovaTek was established on principles of integrity, creativity, and sustainability. The company became a certified B Corporation in 2017, formalizing a mission to promote worldwide health and wellness by fostering the delivery of high-quality, healthy foods through sustainable methods.

SinnovaTek develops and integrates advanced food processing technologies, manufacturing equipment such as thermal processing systems and pumps, while also offering a suite of integration tools. The company operates a precision-scale aseptic copacking facility for rapid prototyping and product launches, and runs a working pilot plant. Its Vitero™ protein‑polyphenol ingredient technology supports product development and piloting services, and the firm provides R&D and engineering support for food‑industry clients.

The company serves the food processing and food technology sectors, working with both established manufacturers and early‑stage ventures. As a member of the Upcycled Food Association since 2020, SinnovaTek also focuses on upcycling excess food through innovative processing infrastructure.

SinnovaTek differentiates itself by making advanced thermal processing and aseptic systems accessible to companies of all sizes, emphasizing that processed foods can retain high nutritional quality. The certified B Corp status and a team of food scientists and engineers with decades of commercialization experience underpin its approach.

about:
Siri Wire Co. operates from Danielson, Connecticut, where it was founded in 1992. The company is a fourth‑generation family business, led by the same family that built it from the ground up, with over 50 years of combined industry experience.

The company manufactures and stocks stainless steel and alloy wire, offering grades such as 302, 304, 316, 17‑7, 302HQ, 303, 316L, 410, 416, 420, and 430. Siri Wire maintains one of the largest domestic stocking positions for electro‑polish‑quality (EPQ) wire in the region, enabling same‑day shipping on many sizes. Through its affiliation with the Tri Star Metals family and the Bender Wire Group, the company draws on two fully operational U.S. production mills, providing domestic melt, DFARS‑compliant, and non‑DFARS material options.

Siri Wire serves medical and surgical device makers, filter‑screen and washer producers, automotive suppliers, aerospace and defense contractors, fastener and cold‑heading shops, and general industrial customers. Typical applications include springs, fasteners, medical equipment, filter screens, washers, and rings.

The company emphasizes mill‑direct quality, competitive pricing, and fast deliveries, backed by ISO 9001 certification and a team that stands behind every order. Its integration into the Tri Star Metals network expands metallurgical and engineering support while deepening inventory availability.

about:
Snap Gourmet Foods, Inc. was founded in 2020 in Cleveland, Ohio, by majority partners Jason Chamoun, Allan Lam, and Lincoln Yee. The trio launched the company during the pandemic with the goal of creating a food oasis in a Cleveland food desert.

The company operates a USDA-inspected facility with more than 40,000 square feet of production space. It manufactures packaged meals, meal kits, sandwiches, wrapped sandwiches, pizzas, and other hand-held foods, offered in shelf-stable, refrigerated, and frozen formats for local and nationwide distribution. Capabilities include sealing food or food components in clear bags, as well as full-service catering and pre-plating foodservice for events ranging from 20 to 1,000 guests.

Snap Gourmet serves private schools, preschools, corporate cafeterias, schools, food banks, and aging agencies. Its meal kits and food boxes are designed to address food insecurity, while its catering division provides chef-inspired cuisine spanning Italian, Latin, Asian, and other styles, accommodating gluten-free, vegan, and other dietary requirements.

The founders, veterans of the food industry who previously founded Symba Brand Solutions and International Food Solutions, state that the company's chief mission is to be a leader in healthy, quality packaged meal solutions, with a focus on quality and a preference for sourcing local ingredients.

The Solar Shield program adds scheduled maintenance, priority scheduling, and detailed reporting to protect production over the system’s 25-year design life.

The company emphasizes a culture of continuous improvement, or Kaizen, with 90 percent of improvement initiatives originating from machine operators. It offers 24/7 emergency service and provides a proprietary solar estimator tool to help customers size their systems. Financing options are available through banks, mortgage companies, power purchase agreements, and manufacturers.

Client verticals include agriculture, education, healthcare, office, public sector, logistics, religious and non-profit organizations, retail, and leisure.

The company emphasizes affordable, reliable, and efficient systems powered by free sunlight, and it offers free solar site evaluations to prospective customers.

It reports millions of feet of subsidy-funded broadband construction completed and more than 5,000 miles of fiber built for government programs such as BEAD and RDOF, supported by a 70 percent in-house W-2 crew model and a fleet representing millions of dollars in equipment investment.

Customers include cable MSOs, internet service providers, and public-sector agencies pursuing federal broadband subsidies. The firm has executed residential drops, large-scale commercial builds, and government-funded infrastructure projects across multiple Southeastern states, with a documented 99.4 percent post-inspection pass rate and the ability to stand up new market branches within 30 to 60 days.

Southeastern Cable positions itself as a single-point accountability partner that lets MSOs focus on their core business rather than contractor oversight. Its stated differentiators include high-performance crews equipped for difficult projects, OSHA-compliant safety programs with weekly training and daily job-hazard analysis, and a philosophy of reliable execution backed by hands-on leadership.

Work is performed in a Nashville shop where the team — including furniture maker Mark Shreve, who has eight years of experience and a portfolio that spans coast-to-coast installations — handles projects from concept through installation. about:
Southern Metal Fabricators is based in Albertville, Alabama. The company was founded in 1991 by Charles Bailey as a two-man shop serving maintenance and light fabrication needs of local industry. It remains family-owned, with Bailey's sons Ashton and Whitton now involved in the business.

The company provides custom carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum fabrication for industrial applications. Its capabilities span design, cutting, forming, welding, finishing, and assembly, with in-house detailing using AutoCAD, MTC Shape Cutting, and Pro Nest software. The 130,000-square-foot high-bay production building sits on six acres of laydown yard and is served by four overhead cranes (up to 10 tons) and a 35-ton gantry crane, enabling fabrication of platforms, handrails, bulk storage tanks, silos, hoppers, ductwork, conveyor structures, and material handling equipment.

Southern Metal Fabricators serves a broad range of industries including agriculture, architecture, automotive, cement, construction, coal and biomass, egg and poultry, feed and grain, iron and steel, mining and quarry, marine, petroleum, paper, plastics, power generation, retail, utilities, and woodworking. Past projects include structural fabrication for ThyssenKrupp's steel manufacturing facility in Alabama.

The company emphasizes a "tool up to handle any custom metal fabrication job, start to finish, right here on the premises" philosophy. Differentiators include pre-assembly and test-running before shipping, a dedicated point of contact for the life of each project, and an in-house quality inspector overseeing every step.

about:
Southern Packaging, LP was founded in 2004 in Venus, Texas, near the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex. The company operates as a limited partnership and has grown into one of the largest distributors of bulk packaging supplies in North America.

The firm stocks more than 1,100 industrial packaging products — including flexible intermediate bulk containers (FIBCs), FIBC liners, multi-wall paper bags, polyethylene bags, woven polypropylene bags, BOPP bags, UN-certified hazardous-material containers, bulk container liners, load-protection supplies, paperboard slip sheets, pallet covers, and stretch film. From its strategically located warehouses it ships to nearly 900 customer locations across the United States, reporting over 100 million bags shipped in 2025. Services include vendor-managed inventory programs, custom package design, and the sale of bag-filling equipment for powders, flakes, and granular products.

Southern Packaging serves manufacturers nationwide across sectors such as agriculture (deer corn and wildlife feed), chemicals (hazardous materials), and general dry-flowable product handling. Its customer base includes over 1,100 clients who rely on the company’s same-day shipping for in-stock items and its relationships with packaging manufacturers.

The company emphasizes its position as the largest on-demand inventory of FIBCs and multi-wall paper packaging in North America, backed by ISO 9001 certification, competitive pricing, and a commitment to reliable on-time delivery.

Product lines encompass the Orlando Collection, Sanibel Series, Vegas Collection, and Cheyenne Series, all offered with customizable finishes and height-adjustable mechanisms.

Space Tables serves senior living communities, assisted living facilities, healthcare providers, and restaurants. Its tables are designed to support independence for residents in home care and nursing home settings, and to withstand the demands of commercial dining environments.

The company's stated mission centers on the belief that dining is a vital social event. By offering customizable, durable tables that can be raised, lowered, and moved, Space Tables aims to help caregivers provide better care and to create products that last for years without replacement.

old_description: Since 2003, SparkFun has been helping turn ideas into reality – whether you’re creating a smart weather station, exploring the frontier of machine learning, building a robot for school or prototyping your first (or tenth) product. about:
SparkFun Electronics was founded in 2003 in Niwot, Colorado. The company began with a mission to make electronics accessible to engineers, hobbyists, and educators through open-source components, tutorials, and documentation.

The company designs and manufactures a wide range of open-source hardware, including sensors, microcontroller development boards, and kits, while also distributing third-party components from brands such as Raspberry Pi, Teensy, and NVIDIA. A dedicated subsidiary, SparkPNT, focuses on high-precision positioning, navigation, and timing products built to be durable, future-proof, and repairable. SparkFun operates with approximately 140 employees and offers a custom kit assembly service for educational workshops and classroom curricula.

SparkFun serves engineers, prototypers, hobbyists, product developers, and educators across industries such as education, robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), environmental monitoring, positioning/navigation/timing (PNT), and artificial intelligence/machine learning. Concrete examples from its partner network include AI robots running on NVIDIA Jetson modules, high-precision GPS boards using u-blox technology, DIY heart-rate monitors, and community hackathons.

The company emphasizes open-source hardware and accessible documentation to lower barriers to emerging technology. Its products are designed to be durable, future-proof, and repairable, and it provides a solderless Qwiic modular ecosystem to simplify prototyping. SparkFun also offers volume pricing, a distributor/reseller program, and free domestic shipping on most orders over $100.

Spotted Owl Timber, Inc. is a locally owned sawmill in Santa Fe, New Mexico, founded in 1991 by David Lindsey. Lindsey, a third-generation sawmill operator born and raised in New Mexico, started the business with a small Wood-Mizer band mill to supply beams and lumber for the growing demand for southwestern-style homes in Santa Fe and northern New Mexico.

The company manufactures natural, custom wood products from locally harvested softwood species including Ponderosa pine, white fir, Douglas fir, and Engelmann spruce. Operations center on a thin-kerf band mill that the company says yields up to 30 percent more lumber per log than traditional circular sawmills, with no chemicals added.

Customers include contractors, private homebuilders, and the general public throughout northern New Mexico.

The business emphasizes sustainable harvesting by local independent loggers, natural materials without chemical treatment, and the efficiency of its thin-kerf band mill technology.

old_description: We have refreshed our brand and website to reflect our evolution as a global engineering partner. Our rebrand aligns our teams, technologies, and customers around a shared commitment to deliver the right design, at the right time, at the optimal cost. about:
Standex Electronics operates from its headquarters in Fairfield, Ohio, as a global platform company that unifies three specialized divisions: Standex Detect, Standex Edge, and Standex Grid. The business traces its roots through generations of innovation in electronic components, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Over time, strategic acquisitions — including Amran and Narayan Powertech, which now anchor the Grid division — have expanded its portfolio into a diversified, vertically integrated operation.

The company designs and manufactures precision-engineered electronic components spanning switching and sensing technologies, power magnetics, and grid solutions. Its product range includes reed switches, relays, sensors, custom transformers, planar transformers, inductors, chokes, EMI components, and low- to medium-voltage instrument transformers. Manufacturing facilities, design centers, and sales offices are distributed across North America, Europe, and Asia, providing local support backed by global resources.

Standex serves mission-critical markets including automotive (passenger, commercial, off-road, construction, and agriculture), aerospace and defense, medical, industrial automation, telecommunications, renewable and alternative energy, and electrical utilities. Customers range from OEMs developing smart-home and transportation systems to utilities modernizing grid infrastructure. The company positions its three divisions to address distinct but complementary needs: Detect for switching and sensing, Edge for magnetics in power conversion, and Grid for instrument transformers and high-voltage components.

Standex says its differentiation lies in the combination of a global footprint with local engineering intimacy, a legacy of innovation across reed switches, magnetics, and power-grid technologies, and a unified operating philosophy — Innovate, Consult, Engineer, Deliver — that guides every program from concept through production.

The shop focuses on custom steel fabrication and production welding, delivering everything from single prototypes to thousand‑unit runs. Its core processes include fixture‑based welding, custom assembly, and large‑scale steel fabrication.

StateFab serves the automotive industry as a long‑time Tier One and Tier Two supplier. Its product portfolio centers on conveyor‑system components: overhead, inverted, skillet, ELPO, paint, door, and cab carriers, as well as line platforms and robot gantries built for tight installation windows. The company also produces skillet frames and custom assemblies for plants across North America.

The company emphasizes repeatability and quality control. A quality manual has been in use since 1997, and certified welders work with dedicated checking fixtures so that each subassembly meets the same standard whether the run is one unit or a thousand. Flexible systems allow the shop to move between large production jobs and small prototype fabrications without changing its workflow.

The company sells and rents a broad range of home medical equipment, including mobility aids such as wheelchairs, scooters, walkers, and power chairs; respiratory devices like oxygen concentrators and nebulizers; hospital beds and patient lifts; power lift chairs; and bathroom safety products such as shower chairs, commodes, and grab bars. old_description: “We must not merely seek business profits but must contribute broadly to society through our business activities.” -Sumitomo Chemical, founded with the dual goals of eliminating pollution and helping increase crop yields, has upheld this founding principle as it has evolved in keeping with the changing times.
about:
Sumitomo Chemical Advanced Technologies, a wholly owned subsidiary of Japan’s Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd., operates from a 50,000-square-foot facility in Phoenix, Arizona. The U.S. entity was formed in 2003 when Sumitomo Chemical acquired the assets of ATMI’s GaAs epitaxial wafer business, building on epitaxial research that dates back to 1971.

The company develops and manufactures compound-semiconductor epitaxial wafers using metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) on 2‑ to 6‑inch substrates, running eleven Aixtron reactors (2600 G3, 2400/2600 G3, and 2800 G4 models) with a stated capacity exceeding 100,000 wafers per year. It also produces super engineering plastics such as LCP, PES, and PPSU under the Sumikasuper and Sumikaexcel brands, compounds Penacolite resins for tire and rubber applications, grinds PES for advanced composites, and formulates photoresists, wet chemicals, polarizing films, and lithium‑battery separators.

Customers span the semiconductor, wireless, automotive, consumer-electronics, solar-energy, medical-device, tire-and-rubber, and composite-materials sectors. The epitaxial foundry supplies HBT, pHEMT, LED, diode, and VCSEL wafers for wireless and optical communications, while engineering plastics and resins serve automotive connectors, industrial components, and medical applications. Photoresist and optical-film products target semiconductor lithography and display manufacturers.

The business was created to strengthen Sumitomo Chemical’s position in the global semiconductor and IT-related materials market, leveraging the parent’s century-old commitment to solving environmental problems through chemistry. The company emphasizes a “Culture of Customer Focus” with goals of zero returns, 100% on-time delivery, and 100% customer satisfaction, backed by ISO 9001, ISO 14001, IATF 16949, and ISO 45001 certifications.

old_description: Superior Machine and Welding is your Alaskan Family owned full service machine shop in Anchorage. We’ve been here on Ship Ave. since 1950 keeping all the industry in the state moving forward and we don’t plan on stopping.
about:
Superior Machine & Welding operates from Anchorage, Alaska, where it has occupied a site on Ship Avenue since 1950. The business began when Jack L. Whitmore purchased a 3,400-square-foot shop and later reclaimed adjacent land from Ship Creek to expand. A 1964 addition brought the facility to 10,000 square feet, adding two Lodge & Shipley oil-country lathes and a five-ton overhead crane. Today the company is owned by WOSB-certified Jantina Lunsford, Whitmore's daughter, continuing the family-owned legacy.

The shop provides full-service machining, welding, and custom fabrication for repair and new-build work. Welding covers TIG, MIG, stick, and brazing in materials from mild steel and aluminum to exotic alloys such as Inconel, Hastelloy, and titanium. The facility also houses 40- and 160-ton hydraulic presses, horizontal and vertical band saws, and a 3D CNC programming station.

Customers span Alaska's marine, heavy-equipment, oilfield, construction, and government sectors. The shop regularly repairs cast-iron components, rebuilds shafts and bores to OEM specifications for marine and heavy-equipment applications, and machines oilfield directional-drill timing rings. Clients range from federal and state agencies to corporations and private individuals.

The company emphasizes that its local presence eliminates the long lead times and high freight costs of sourcing from the lower 48. It backs every job with a guarantee against workmanship defects and highlights its multi-generational machinist experience—over 100 combined years—as a differentiator for tackling complex geometries and difficult materials that other shops decline.

Customers include Porsche Brooklyn for branded merchandise, Oliver Charles for bootstrapped fashion lines, Tigerbob for artistic knits, and Ministry of Supply for built‑to‑order production. The platform integrates directly with Shopify for real‑time order tracking and drop shipping.

The company was created to give brands what they want, when they want it: no minimums, full transparency, and domestic production that blends heritage craftsmanship with advanced software. Its founders aimed to eliminate the inventory risk and hidden costs that plague traditional manufacturing, offering a sustainable, flexible alternative for brands of any size.

This integrated approach, combined with the proprietary automated line, aims to ensure batch-to-batch consistency and bridge traditional botanical knowledge with modern pharmaceutical validation.

Tekin, Inc. operates from McCall, Idaho, where it designs and manufactures electronic speed controls, brushless and brushed motors, servos, LiHV batteries, and proprietary connectors for radio-control vehicles. The product line spans multiple ESC platforms — including the RX8 GEN3 for 1:8-scale racing, the RSX Pro for modified competition, the compact RS GEN3 series, the BXR brushed reversing controller, and the RX4 HardBox rock-crawling unit — alongside the Eliminator and GEN4 brushless motor families, the GEN4 SPEC-R spec-class motors, 5-Slot brushed crawler motors, full-aluminum-housing servos with digital magnetic position encoding, and POWER CELL LiHV battery packs in 1S–4S configurations. old_description: Texas Instruments (TI) is a semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Texas. Produces analog and embedded processing chips used in a wide range of applications including automotive, industrial controls and consumer electronics.
about:
Texas Instruments traces its roots to 1930 when Geophysical Service Inc., a small oil and gas exploration firm, opened in Dallas, Texas. The company pivoted during World War II, applying signal‑processing expertise to submarine detection and radar, and established an electronics equipment laboratory in 1946. In the 1950s it reorganized as Texas Instruments Inc., entering the semiconductor industry with the invention of the silicon transistor in 1954 and Jack Kilby’s breakthrough integrated circuit in 1958.

TI designs, manufactures, and sells analog and embedded processing semiconductors. Its portfolio exceeds 80,000 products, including analog ICs, embedded processors, and wireless transceivers. The company runs a global manufacturing network that includes 300 mm wafer fabs powered entirely by renewable electricity, producing tens of billions of chips annually. With roughly 33,000 employees worldwide, TI handles everything from process technology and design through packaging, test, and delivery.

The company serves more than 100,000 customers across automotive, industrial, consumer electronics, communications, data‑center, and medical‑equipment markets. Its chips power vehicle electrification and safety systems, factory automation, smartphones, optical networking gear, and life‑saving medical devices. TI emphasizes supply‑chain reliability, promising delivery “in any geopolitical environment.”

TI’s stated mission is to make electronics more affordable through semiconductors. It operates with three long‑term ambitions: act like owners who will own the company for decades, adapt to a changing world, and be a company its people are proud of. Differentiators cited include a 40,000‑patent portfolio, over $2 billion in annual R&D spending, and a comprehensive analog‑and‑embedded product breadth that lets engineers consolidate sourcing.

old_description: Offering custom compounding to meet customer’s needs since 1973
about:
The Plastics Group of America (TPG) is headquartered in Woonsocket, Rhode Island. The company traces its roots to 1973 when Bob Lebeaux founded Ralco Industries, Inc., a one-man operation buying and selling scrap plastics. In 1978 the firm added a grinder, baler, extruder and tractor‑trailer to enter recycling, and in 1980 began custom compounding reinforced thermoplastics under the Polifil® trade name. The business was renamed The Plastics Group of America in 1988, consolidating Ralco, Polifil® and the Transcontinental Polymers recycling unit. Today the company remains family‑led, with Lebeaux family members holding key executive and operational roles.

TPG operates more than 300,000 square feet of manufacturing space in Woonsocket, including the former Jules Desurmont Mill complex acquired in 2012. With a workforce of 60‑plus employees and annual revenue exceeding $50 million, the company custom‑compounds mineral‑ and glass‑filled polypropylene resins to precise mechanical, thermal and physical specifications. Its on‑site quality laboratory performs melt index, Izod, flexural, tensile, DSC, moisture, ash, Gardner impact and color testing on every batch. Beyond compounding, TPG provides recycling and toll‑processing services, color matching at no charge, and acts as a resin broker and distributor with stock ready for shipment.

The company serves processors in appliance, automotive, construction, consumer housewares, furniture, industrial/institutional/electronic, medical and personal care, packaging, and pump/pool/spa/irrigation markets. Customers include injection molders, extruders and blow‑molders who rely on TPG’s Polifil® resins for consistent performance in demanding applications.

TPG emphasizes its asset‑based manufacturing model, ISO 9001 certification and an on‑site testing lab as differentiators that enable tight lot‑to‑lot consistency whether the order is 100 pounds or one million pounds. The firm also highlights its recycling expertise, free color compounding, and a technical insights library that helps customers optimize molding processes.

The Wooden Nickel operates from Arab, Alabama, where it builds custom live‑edge furniture from locally sourced hardwood slabs. The company does not publish a founding year or ownership structure, but its blog posts describe a shop that began with a focus on honest craftsmanship — turning rough logs into dining tables, desks, and workstations meant to last generations.

Production centers on kiln‑dried slabs sourced from tree services and loggers. Each piece moves through stabilization, flattening, sanding, and, when needed, resin filling of cracks or knots before receiving multiple hand‑applied finish coats. Steel bases — ranging from simple dark‑finished legs to adjustable‑height desk frames made from high‑tolerance steel — are fitted in‑house. The shop handles one‑off commissions and larger custom runs alike, though it does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Customers span residential and commercial segments. A Marshall County family commissioned a three‑generation dining table; remote workers order wide slab workstations with cable management; local businesses have requested reinforced tables for offices, break rooms, and public areas that endure daily wear. The company notes that the same durability valued by commercial clients appeals to homeowners as well.

The Wooden Nickel positions itself against mass‑produced furniture, emphasizing “no templates, no shortcuts” and a slow, deliberate process — “if it wouldn’t hold up in our own homes, it doesn’t leave the shop.” The stated goal is furniture built for real life: sturdy, honest, and meant to outlast a warranty card.

name: Tonka Electronics
old_description: ​Tonka Electronics, Inc., was founded on September 1, 1976 as a Manufacturer's Representative and stocking Distributor for the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly industry.  We are a woman owned, small business incorporated in the state of Minnesota.
about:
Tonka Electronics, Inc. was founded on September 1, 1976 in Bloomington, Minnesota as a manufacturer's representative and stocking distributor for the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly industry. The woman-owned small business was incorporated in Minnesota by founder Mike DeLadi, who emphasized a "no slogans, just service" philosophy. Initially focused on representing capital equipment lines, the company expanded into stocking consumables required by that equipment.

Today Tonka operates as a focused distributor specializing in soldering and cleaning products, maintaining a fully stocked warehouse of leaded and lead-free solder bar, wire, and paste, along with fluxes, flux additives, solder masks, and cleaning agents. The company also offers its own SpliceRite line of SMT tape splicing products, cover tape extenders, and carrier tape cutting tools, plus SmartDry intelligent dry storage systems for SMT component reels and trays. Services include manufacturability assessment, process design, technical training, solder analysis, and low-cost resharpening. Tonka supplies spare parts and accessories for Electrovert equipment such as spray fluxers, convection preheaters, chip waves, and nitrogen nozzles, and provides test solutions for Ionograph and OmegaMeter ionic contamination testers.

The company serves the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly sector across its manufacturer's representative territory of Minnesota, North and South Dakota, northwest Wisconsin, and occasionally Iowa. As a distributor, it ships nationwide to electronics manufacturers, including medical device producers who use fine hard wire cutting tools. Customers range from contract manufacturers to OEMs implementing new production lines.

Tonka differentiates itself through deep technical expertise in soldering and cleaning processes, offering both equipment integration support and a broad inventory of consumables available for immediate shipment. The founder's service-first approach remains central, with the company providing free samples of SpliceRite products and hands-on assistance with process development.

about:
Founded in 1989 in Riverside, California, Trademark Plastics, Inc. (TPI) operates as a U.S.-based contract manufacturer specializing in custom plastic injection molding for the medical device, life science, and diagnostic industries.

The company runs a 100,000-square-foot facility housing 51 injection molding machines ranging from 6 to 610 tons, supported by two ISO Class 8 cleanrooms and two controlled-environment white rooms. Its vertically integrated services span scientific molding (RJG-certified), mold design and validation, tool fabrication and lifecycle maintenance, assembly, kitting, packaging, and full IQ/OQ/PQ process validations. A staff of over 100 employees serves a global customer base that includes eight of the world's top 30 medical device OEMs, with prototyping available in as few as five days using aluminum or steel tooling.

TPI focuses on the healthcare sector, serving medical device, pharmaceutical, diagnostics, electronics, and consumer product markets. Its product portfolio includes custom medical components, in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) supplies, lab supplies, and consumer goods. The company emphasizes regulatory compliance, holding ISO 13485 certification, MedAccred accreditation, and adherence to FDA 21 CFR Part 820.

Since its inception, TPI has pursued a vision of achieving the highest attainable manufacturing standards. The firm differentiates itself through vertical integration from design-for-manufacturing through distribution, in-house metrology including a ZEISS Metrotom 800 CT scanner, and dedicated program management for each project.

name: Troy Brook Visions Fine Art Furniture Gallery and Studio
old_description: Tucked among the rolling hills of beautiful Litchfield, Connecticut is the studio and gallery of Troy Brook Visions, Inc., Makers of Fine Furniture. Master Artisan Daniel Gugnoni designs and creates exquisite custom handcrafted fine art furniture.
about:
Troy Brook Visions operates from a red barn studio and gallery on Clark Road in Litchfield, Connecticut. The company was founded in 1993 by Daniel Gugnoni, a sculptor turned furniture maker, who established the business on the Shaker principles of hard work, honesty, and pride in craftsmanship. Barbara Gugnoni joined the venture in 1996, bringing a background in advertising and sales to manage client relations and the finishing process.

The studio produces one-of-a-kind and custom fine art furniture, each piece designed and handcrafted by Daniel Gugnoni. The work emphasizes pure forms and clean lines, allowing the natural character of each wood board to guide the design. Barbara applies a twelve-step hand-rubbed finish to protect and enhance the surfaces. The operation is deliberately small-scale, with no mass production; the barn houses both the workshop and a second-floor gallery where completed pieces are displayed.

Troy Brook Visions serves private clients seeking heirloom-quality furniture, as well as collectors and visitors who attend the gallery or the craft shows where the company exhibits. The firm has shown at the American Craft Council Shows, the Paradise City Arts Festival, the Philadelphia Invitational Furniture Show, the Fine Furnishings Show, and Crafts America. Clients work directly with Daniel on custom commissions, while the gallery offers ready-made pieces for immediate purchase.

The company distinguishes itself by rejecting volume manufacturing in favor of artistic creation, a philosophy captured in the statement "Never manufacturing product, always creating art." The Shaker-inspired founding ethos and the practice of letting the wood dictate the form remain central to the studio's identity.

about:
True Weld Metal Fabrication operates from Aurora, Colorado, serving the Denver metropolitan area. The family-owned shop traces its roots to a home garage where the founder began welding more than two decades ago, eventually expanding into a mobile-and-shop operation that covers residential, commercial, and agricultural sites across the region.

The company provides on-site mobile welding and in-shop custom fabrication, working with mild steel, aluminum, and stainless steel. Services include structural welding for beams, columns, and mezzanines; trailer and equipment repairs; custom gates, fences, and handrails; and code-conscious structural fabrication. The owner-operator performs every weld, with no subcontracting, and the shop handles both one-off pieces and repeat production for commercial clients.

It runs 36 injection molding machines ranging from 60 to 1,000 tons, equipped with servo-robotics and nitrogen gas-assist, and builds nearly 100 new molds each year — from single-cavity prototypes to 64-cavity high-production tools. More than 50 certified resins are stocked in-house, including PVC, nylon, polyethylene, and polycarbonate, supported by an internal material testing lab and rapid prototyping capability.

Its original customer base was the fence and deck industry, where it now offers over 950 accessory products and introduces at least 20 new items annually.

The company emphasizes its U.S.-based manufacturing, in-house tooling and engineering, rapid prototyping printed in hours, and a three-warehouse distribution network as key differentiators. Its stated mission is to lead the industry in design, manufacturing, and distribution of plastic injection molding products by setting benchmarks for quality, service, and competitive pricing.

about:
United & Turtle Mountain Communications, headquartered in Langdon, North Dakota, traces its roots to February 1952 when the United Telephone Cooperative was organized by local residents to bring telephone service to rural northeastern North Dakota. West. Today the company operates from offices in Langdon, Bottineau, and Rolla.

The company provides high‑speed broadband internet, digital TV, digital telephone, and security services to residential and business customers across its service area. It owns and operates more than 330 miles of fiber‑optic cable and has deployed fiber‑to‑the‑home in Langdon, Bottineau, Walhalla, Rolette, and Rolla. Through its partnerships, it also provides long‑distance service to six other North Dakota carriers via North Dakota Long Distance (NDLD) and special‑circuit engineering through ND Telecom. The network includes Motorola MITS mobile systems, Stromberg Carlson DCO switches, and a CopperCom soft switch for CALEA compliance.

Customers include rural households, small and large businesses, school districts, and government agencies served via the Dakota Carrier Network. The company has constructed towers for Verizon Wireless in Rolla and Bottineau, and previously supported the U.S. Department of Defense’s Safeguard Complex at Nekoma. Its United Telephone Educational Foundation has awarded nearly $450,000 in scholarships since inception.

The cooperative’s stated mission is to keep rural North Dakota communities connected so they can work and thrive. As a designated Smart Rural Community provider, it emphasizes local ownership, community reinvestment, and the deployment of advanced fiber infrastructure to bridge the digital divide.
